key_takeaways: A closure captures the binding, not the value; it reads the current value when it runs.
let creates a binding per loop iteration; var shares one binding across the loop.
Choose what to capture on purpose: a fresh binding, a parameter, or a mutable box you update.

exercise.title: Rewrite one stale closure three ways
exercise.instructions: Take a stale-closure bug and write three versions: a fresh binding per iteration, a parameter that freezes the value, and a mutable box read at call time. Comment what each sees when the outer variable changes later and prove it with a transcript.
exercise.deliverable: Three annotated versions and a printed transcript showing what each reports after the outer variable changes.
hints: Run each version with node and change the outer variable before calling the closures.
A parameter is a new binding on every call; that is the snapshot form.
If you need the newest value, read a box or re-subscribe; do not rely on re-creating the closure by accident.

questions.prompt: Handlers created in `for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++)` all return 3. Why?
choices: var creates one function-scoped binding shared by every closure
questions.correct_answer: var creates one function-scoped binding shared by every closure
questions.explanation: Every closure reads the same binding, which holds 3 when the loop ends.

questions.prompt: What does `for (let j …)` change for closures created inside the loop?
choices: Nothing; let and var behave alike in loops
Each iteration gets its own binding, so each closure sees a distinct value
Closures cannot be created in let loops
questions.correct_answer: Each iteration gets its own binding, so each closure sees a distinct value
questions.explanation: A fresh let binding per iteration is why handlers report 0, 1, 2.

choices: 0, the value when read was created
5, the current value of the captured binding
questions.correct_answer: 5, the current value of the captured binding
questions.explanation: Closures read bindings at call time, not creation time.

questions.prompt: A debounced search function keeps using an old API base URL after settings changed. Explain the mechanism and two fixes.
questions.correct_answer: The debounced function closed over the configuration binding or object that held the old URL when it was built, so it keeps reading that captured value. Fix by reading the configuration at call time through a box or getter that you update deliberately, or by rebuilding the debounced function whenever the configuration changes so it captures the new binding.
questions.explanation: Stale closures capture old bindings; read current state on purpose or rebuild.
questions.learning_objective: Diagnose a stale closure in real code

questions.prompt: Why does passing a value as a parameter freeze it while capturing an outer variable does not?
questions.correct_answer: A parameter is a new binding created for each call and initialized with the value passed in, so the closure captures that private binding and no later assignment to the outer variable touches it. Capturing an outer variable captures the shared binding, which later assignments change.
questions.explanation: Parameters create fresh bindings; outer captures share bindings.
questions.learning_objective: Distinguish parameter capture from outer capture
